data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 never answers the second, distinguishing part of the problem: it must identify what evidence within a single evaluation would separate a genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance that tracks the right answer. The target defines reliability as accuracy/truth and attacks the panel as mere precision, but it supplies no within-evaluation evidentiary test (e.g., checklist-followers being right for checklist-derivable reasons vs. right-by-luck, or error-pattern analysis showing the panel fails exactly where the checklist is inapplicable). Its counterconditions only say when the expert might lose, not what evidence would distinguish the two modes. The one counterexample it offers is a task-type edge case, not an evaluation-internal discriminator. Thus it omits the precise distinguishing-evidence requirement.
